title: Drugs affecting calcium and bone: vitamin D and analogues, antiresorptives and anabolics

groups.title: Vitamin D and analogues
groups.desc: ↑ gut absorption and renal reabsorption of calcium AND phosphate. Each step down needs less activation.

drugs.name: Ergocalciferol (D2)
drugs.agents: plant sources; stored in liver, fat, muscle

drugs.name: Cholecalciferol (D3)
drugs.agents: skin + sun, animal sources, fortified food

lines.label: Pick when:
lines.text: secondary hyperparathyroidism in stage 3–4 CKD with low 25-hydroxyvitamin D.

lines.label: Pick when:
lines.text: PTH must be shut off fast (hypoparathyroidism); works without renal function.

after.label: Too much:
after.text: hypercalcemia. Acute nausea, vomiting, anorexia, weakness; chronic renal impairment, soft-tissue calcification, hypertension.

groups.title: Antiresorptive
groups.desc: Suppress the osteoclast to stop bone loss. All lower serum calcium.

drugs.name: Bisphosphonates
drugs.agents: alendronate (oral), zoledronate (IV); potency ↑ with each generation
drugs.moa: Bind hydroxyapatite → taken up by the resorbing osteoclast → block the mevalonate pathway → osteoclast apoptosis.

lines.label: Elimination:
lines.text: renal, excreted unchanged (active), so they accumulate when kidneys fail. Not metabolized; also retained in bone for years.

lines.label: Avoid:
lines.text: CrCl < 30, esophageal abnormality, hypocalcemia. Empty stomach, water, upright 30 min. IV: flu-like symptoms, nephrotoxicity.

drugs.name: RANKL inhibitor: denosumab
drugs.agents: human monoclonal antibody; only one in Canada
drugs.moa: Binds RANKL from osteoblasts and osteocytes → blocks osteoclast activation, differentiation and survival. Reversible on stopping.

lines.label: Elimination:
lines.text: does NOT depend on the kidneys, so it is the drug of choice in poor renal function.

lines.label: Avoid:
lines.text: immunosuppression, hypocalcemia. Higher ONJ risk than bisphosphonates, but it falls after stopping.

after.text: Also antiresorptive, named but not developed: SERMs, hormone replacement therapy, calcitonin.

drugs.name: Teriparatide (rhPTH 1–34)
drugs.moa: Intermittent spikes build bone; sustained PTH resorbs it. Also ↑ calcitriol, ↑ osteoblast survival, ↑ renal Ca²⁺ reabsorption, phosphaturic.

lines.label: Elimination:
lines.text: metabolized by the liver, excreted in the urine, hence the CrCl < 30 contraindication.

lines.label: Avoid:
lines.text: hypercalcemia, CrCl < 30, metabolic bone disease. Transient hypotension, dizziness, leg cramps. Osteosarcoma in rats only (boxed warning removed).

drugs.name: Sclerostin inhibitor: romosozumab
drugs.moa: Sclerostin inhibits formation and promotes resorption, so blocking it ↑ formation and ↓ resorption at once.

lines.label: Elimination:
lines.text: not covered in the lecture. A monoclonal antibody, so broken down like other proteins rather than filtered by the kidney.

lines.label: Avoid:
lines.text: hypocalcemia. The cardiovascular signal is the reason to hesitate.

after.text: Also bone-forming, named but not developed: fluoride. Elsewhere on the calcium loop: cinacalcet (calcium-sensing receptor), thiazide diuretics (↑ renal Ca²⁺ reabsorption).
